To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DHA prevents C12:10, C12:12 CLA-induced NAFLD in mice by altering hepatic expression of genes regulating fatty acid metabolism, and the effects of DHA are mediated through PPARγ and PPARα activation.
docosahexaenaenoic acid prevents the development of nonalcoholic fatty disease in mice fed trans-10,cis-12-CLA, by altering expression of genes regulating fatty acid oxidation and synthesis.

docosahexaenoin acid supplementation prevents CLA-induced nonalcoholic steatohepatitis by reducing hepatic expression of lipogenic genes and enhancing hepatic expression of genes regulating fatty acid oxidation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of docosahexaenoeic acid (DHA) in the prevention of trans-10, trans-12 conjugated linoleic (CLA) induced NAFLD and the mechanisms involved.
the effects of dietary CLA and DHA on the liver of mice.
the development and evaluation of a new class of drugs that are capable of preventing or treating obesity and related disorders such as nonalcoholic fatty-liver disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the term "conjugated" for linoleic acid was a mistake and should not be used in the future.
CLA has a potential for use as a dietary supplement for the prevention of cancer.
the use of the drug is not justified in the absence of a clear diagnosis of a specific disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that docosahexaenoi acid (DHA) prevents the development of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease induced by trans-10,cis-12-conjugate linoleic acid (CLA) in a murine model.
we have shown that DHA can prevent C12:10 CLA-induced NASH by reducing hepatic lipid accumulation and inflammation.
we have shown that docosahexaenoi acid prevents trans 10, cis 12-conjugated linoelic acid-induced non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have identified a novel role for the transcription factor PGC1alpha in regulating the response of skeletal muscle to exercise and that this response is dependent on the presence of a specific amino acid in the PGC1alpha gene.
we have a better understanding of what is going on in the body when we eat CLA, and how we can use that information to our advantage.
we have a potential new therapeutic strategy for the treatment of fatty liver disease.
